newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Red Army famed for deadly attacks.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Red Army famed for deadly attacks.

text.p: Japan's Red Army was once one of the world"s most feared guerrilla groups for its ability to stage deadly and spectacular attacks from plane hijackings to hostage-taking.
Led by a 51-year-old woman, Fusako Shigenobu, who is still at large, the group was born out of the 1960s anti-Vietnam War movement and believed in the total destruction of capitalism.
Its members fought at home against the presence of U.S. forces in Japan and then in the early 1970s took their struggle overseas.
They backed their rhetoric with a mix of ruthless violence and careful planning which often kept them one step ahead of international law enforcement agencies who have pursued them for decades.

After the winding down of the United States military's involvement in Vietnam, the Red Army turned its attention to the Middle East, becoming implacable foes of Israel and supporters of Palestinian independence.
Intelligence sources say the group, which once numbered in the hundreds, has now dwindled to only about 40 active members who are scattered in hideouts around the world.
Some were arrested while many melted back into Japanese society as their revolutionary fervour cooled.
The following are some of the group's most infamous attacks:
Feb 1971 -- Leader Fusako Shigenobu travels to Lebanon and links up with the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP).

May 1972 -- Three members attack Lod airport in Tel Aviv with grenades and machine guns. In the Japanese Red Army-PFLP operation, 26 people including two Japanese Red Army members were killed and 78 people were injured. The only surviving Red Army member was Kozo Okamoto.

July 1973 -- Japanese Red Army member leads four PFLP guerrillas in hijacking a Japan Airlines (JAL) plane over the Netherlands, forcing it to land in Dubai and then Libya, where all passengers and crew are released and plane is blown up.
Jan 1974 - Members blow up storage tanks at oil refinery in Singapore.
Sept 1974 -- Japanese Red Army seizes French Embassy in The Hague, taking the French ambassador hostage. They win the release of one imprisoned comrade and flee to Syria.

Aug 1975 -- Japanese Red Army members seize U.S. consul, Swedish charge d"affaires and 51 other hostages in building housing U.S., Swedish, Japanese and Canadian embassies in Kuala Lumpur. They win release of five imprisoned comrades and fly to Libya with them.

Sept 1977 -- Five Japanese Red Army members hijack Japan Airlines airliner over India and force it to land in Dhaka. Hijackers fly to Algeria after Japanese government meets their demand for release of six prisoners and $6 million.
May 1985 -- Okamoto freed after 14 years' imprisonment in an exchange of prisoners between Israeli and Palestinian forces.
May, 1986 -- Japanese Red Army fires mortar rounds at the embassies of Japan, Canada and the United States in Jakarta.
June, 1987 -- Japanese Red Army fires mortar rounds at embassies of Britain and the United States in Rome.
April 1988 -- Japanese Red Army bombs U.S. military recreational club in Naples, Italy, killing five.
